findings.issue:
A kept token with no 3-character anchor collapses, so ranges are still lost on Tab with no race. This is not in any Known limit. oldText under 3 characters returns the trimmed hunk (line 273), a gap whose old side is under 3 is never searched (lines 315-316, 329-330), and a text with no shared gram finds no block (line 341). Measured: Tab on all 500 one-character lines (999 characters): 499 of 500 collapse. Tab on a 200-line note where every third line is 'x': all 67 of those lines collapse, while the other 133 keep their place. mapTextSpan('1
2
3
4
5', indented text, 4, 5) gives {28, 28}. 'OK' to 'Not OK at all' and 'v2' to 'release v2 now' collapse too, which also hits a carried range in a merge. The edit is one keystroke, the characters are all still there, and a native range stays collapsed. Item 1 of the request names Tab and Shift+Tab on all lines, and FR-3 says ranges must survive.
findings.fix: Add a second bounded pass for gaps with no block or an old side under MIN_MATCH_LENGTH: find the old token in the new gap nearest the diagonal, or align by whole lines first, charging the meter and staying deterministic. Add Tab and Shift+Tab tests on one-character lines and a test for 'OK' to 'Not OK at all'; the test 'drops matches shorter than three' pins the current floor and must be revisited with the plan.

findings.issue: An addition beside a word can land inside it, and the range then widens over all the added text. The prefix or suffix seed keeps letters the addition shares with the word, and the last-gap trim (line 367) does the same, so the insertion sits strictly inside the range. Measured with mapTextSpan: 'foo Bid' to 'foo Before Bid' styles 'Before Bid'; T to 'Bid request timeout 1 second or 120ms' styles '1 second or 120ms' instead of '120ms'; in the 326-character prose, pasting 'daily ' before 'dashboard' styles 'daily dashboard' and 'escalation ' before 'engineer' styles 'escalation engineer'; 'Bid request' to 'Bid and kid request' styles 'Bid and kid'; 'the red car' with ' and bed' after 'red' styles 'red and bed'. change_plan.md line 40 names this as the third cause and treats it as fixed, but the code only fixes it when the suffix run beats the prefix run or the word is the whole text. The test 'a word added in front that starts with the same letter' (packages/element/tests/textRanges.test.ts:236) uses only the whole-text case, so it passes on this defect. This breaks the FR-3 boundary rule and the run's own bar that the styled text is the same word.
findings.fix: After the gaps are built, slide each pure insertion or deletion within its repeat window and prefer a position on a whitespace or line boundary, deterministically, at a cost bounded by the hunk length and charged to the meter. Add tests with text before and after the word: the cases above on prose and on a long text. Keep 'abc' to 'abcabc' as it is.

findings.issue: The budget accounting has no test that can fail on it. In scratch mutants run through the real test files, removing any one charge left textRanges.test.ts and reconcile.textRanges.test.ts green: meter.left -= back + 1 (textDiff.ts:97), meter.left -= length (:121), meter.left -= 1 (:147) and meter.left -= indexWork (:282). 'hostile text stops at the budget' only checks that the meter ends between 0 and -200,002, and the other charges still reach that window. Removing the forward or backward charge lets real scan work go unmetered, so NFR-2 could be lost with a green suite. The code as written is bounded: a 100,000-character hostile diff took 33 ms and overshot by 1 unit.
findings.fix: Assert exact meter values on small fixed inputs, one input per charge: an index-only case, a miss-only case, a case dominated by backward extension and one dominated by forward extension. Keep the hostile test for the rebuild and the overshoot bound.

findings.issue: Two of the four surrogate guards are untested. With the block-end guard (textDiff.ts:128-133) or the trim-end guard (:246-249) removed, both test files stay green. 'never splits a surrogate pair' changes only the low unit, and 'a block never starts inside a surrogate pair' covers only the block start. The code itself is right: 20,000 fuzzed cases with emoji and lone surrogates, on full and starved meters, gave no failed rebuild and no hunk edge inside a pair.
findings.fix: Add diffText('a😀b', 'a🨀b') expecting one hunk {1,3,1,3} for the trim-end guard, and a case such as 'Qabcde😀Z' to 'Rabcde😁Y' for a block ending on a shared high surrogate.

findings.issue: Other planned behaviour survives its removal. These mutants left both test files green: scanning each gap left to right instead of from the middle, though the plan names this as the fix for repeated lines and this test uses only 100 lines; a stride of best.length * 3, which can skip a longer run; no first-gap trim (textDiff.ts:366); no fast path for a typed character (textDiff.ts:275), where no test asserts the meter is untouched; and no hunksByText cache (textRangeMerge.ts:140), though the plan says each distinct text is paid for once.
findings.fix: Add a test on about 1,000 identical lines, one where a longer run sits between stride positions, 'x cdefg' to 'xy cdefg' for the first-gap trim, a meter-unchanged assertion on a typed character, and a merge test where records share one origin text and diffText is called once.

findings.issue: The code does worse than the 'diff budget is per element' Known limit says. change_plan.md line 42 says only hostile or very long text reaches the budget, and that the longest ordinary case, Tab on a 100,000-character note, used 1.81M of 2M. That holds for unique lines, not for ordinary repeated notes. Measured Tab on all lines: 50,000 characters of one repeated line used 2.00M and 1,825 of 1,852 lines collapsed (30,000 was fine at 1.86M); a repeated paragraph wrapped at 58 lost 146 of 1,017 lines at 60,000 and 1,319 of 1,356 at 80,000; word-list lines at 100,000 lost 1,673 of 1,962. Random unique lines first fail near 200,000. The loss is a cliff, not a gradual decline.
findings.fix: Make repeated re-scans cheaper, for example by lowering the search cost of a gap on repetitive text, or correct the Known limit with these real thresholds and the cliff behaviour so the person accepts what actually happens.

findings.issue: drawStyledTextLines sets context.direction per piece (line 521) but the branch for a line with no run does not reset it. On an element with mixed-direction text, an unstyled line after a styled line inherits the last piece's direction, so neutral characters at its edges can reorder. The plan's bidi Known limit says lines with no visible run take today's path.
findings.fix: Pass the element's direction in and set context.direction to it in the no-layout branch. Add a draw-call test that records context.direction for an unstyled line after a line with an rtl piece.

findings.issue: expect(diffText('ab', 'bb')).toBeDefined() cannot fail: diffText always returns an array, and nothing uses the result.
findings.fix: Delete the line, or assert the exact hunk the test depends on.

findings.issue: Three record literals with their own ad-hoc type and an 'as ExcalidrawTextRange' cast (lines 149-178, 284-303, 305-324) repeat what createTextRange in textRanges.ts already does, including omitting undefined keys.
findings.fix: Build all three with createTextRange and drop the casts.

passing: Hunks rebuild the new text and stay in order: by reading, and on the 20,000-case fuzz above; no surrogate pair is split.
Work is bounded: 33 ms on the hostile 100,000-character diff, 2 ms to map 1,024 records through its 1,084 hunks, 121 ms for 300 long distinct origins on one meter.
FR-19: 400 three-way races in all 6 orders gave no divergence and no stale offset.
Random multi-edit prose: at least 99.1% of untouched words land exactly in every scenario; the non-exact cases sampled trace to word-edge slides like finding 2 or to repeated text.
Replacing 'stops at the cell cap' was right: it pinned the defect, and 'an empty meter returns the trimmed hunk' keeps its input and one-hunk result through the real limit.
The Gate 3 budget test exists, keeps 5010, and fails on a mutant that drops the highest-first order or the shared meter.
The three Gate 3 decisions are in the plan (lines 41, 42 and 47); apart from findings 2, 6 and 7, the plan matches the code read.
